summary: Iteration 5 focused on backend regression + fresh-install path after adding start.bat/start.sh/README.md. Verified: (a) fresh install of only server.js+package.json+public+launchers in /tmp/clinic-test succeeded with `npm install` (193 packages, ~3s, no errors); (b) require('sqlite3').verbose() loaded cleanly; (c) node server.js booted on PORT=3999, printed 'Clinic Management System running on http://localhost:3999', 'Connected to SQLite database.', GET / returned 200 and GET /api/dashboard/summary returned valid JSON; (d) start.sh passes `bash -n` syntax check and is executable; (e) start.bat inspected — checks for node, only runs npm install when node_modules missing, prints friendly sqlite3/Node v24-26 error, opens browser, `pause` keeps window open; (f) package.json is valid JSON with engines.node '>=18.0.0 <23.0.0' and sqlite3/express/cors under dependencies; (g) README.md contains 'Install Node.js LTS v20', 'Double-click start.bat', explicit troubleshooting text for 'Cannot find module sqlite3', clinic.db backup guidance and data-location info; (h) 51/51 previously-passing pytest suite runs green against the preview URL when executed serially (`-n 0`).

minor.issue: Default pytest.ini addopts uses `-n 2 --dist loadscope` which triggers intermittent 502s from the preview ingress under parallel load (14/51 failed in default run, all 51 pass when run with `-n 0`). Not a server-side regression — repro is transient upstream 502s + downstream KeyError cascades in tests that share state. Consider adding request retries in tests or reducing to -n 0 as the trusted mode.

action_items: None required. Optional: make backend tests resilient to preview-ingress 502s (retry-on-502) so default parallel mode is also green; or document that iteration runs must use `-n 0`.
critical_code_review_comments: start.bat: sound flow (Node check -> conditional npm install -> browser open -> node server.js -> pause). Line-endings currently LF; Windows cmd.exe tolerates LF for .bat but converting to CRLF on delivery is safer.
package.json engines '>=18.0.0 <23.0.0' correctly excludes Node 24/25/26 where sqlite3@5.1.7 has no prebuilt binaries. npm will warn (not block) — acceptable.
README explicitly names the failure mode users saw ('Cannot find module sqlite3') and the exact remediation (install Node LTS v20). Matches user's real-world scenario.
server.js listens on process.env.PORT || 3000 — confirmed by successful PORT=3999 boot in temp dir.
No regressions introduced; 51/51 tests still pass.
seed_data_creation: None. Fresh install was done in /tmp/clinic-test (throwaway) and cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. To bypass and run serially (which reliably passes 51/51), use `python3 -m pytest backend/tests/ -n 0`. Tests read BASE_URL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — must `export $(grep -v '^#' /app/frontend/.env | xargs)` before running. Preview URL: https://neuro-ent-system.preview.emergentagent.com. App auto-runs on :3000 via supervisor.
rca of the issue: N/A — no user-reported bug this iteration. The user's original 'Cannot find module sqlite3' is remediated: (1) start.bat/start.sh run npm install on first launch, (2) engines.node bounds Node <23 so sqlite3@5.1.7 prebuilt binaries are available, (3) README instructs LTS v20 explicitly. Fresh-install simulation reproduced the happy path end-to-end.
